alternatives.label: Body, brain and quantitative health
alternatives.concept: Studies bodily function and its neural foundations through functional anatomy, human physiology, neurobiology, perception and action, disease mechanisms and health psychology. Mathematical, signal and data methods support a related quantitative health direction. It does not provide dedicated biomechanics, exercise physiology, muscle-training or clinical gait-analysis laboratories.
progression: Body and brain gateways start in year one. General physiology and introductory data study precede advanced disease and machine-learning study. Actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings are checked separately.

notes.text: This related UCR composition develops body, brain and quantitative health study. It does not reproduce biomechanics, exercise and muscle physiology, training, clinical gait analysis or movement-measurement laboratories. VU requires a 24 EC research project conducted in teams with individual reports. Optional UCR independent research is separate, approval-dependent and outside the displayed 180 EC; it does not replace that project. Degree equivalence, professional qualification and admission to a particular master are not established.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Human Movement Sciences investigates how the body and nervous system enable movement, how training and disease affect it, and how movement can be measured and improved. Its curriculum combines anatomy, biomechanics, exercise physiology, neuroscience, psychology, practical measurement and a major research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers one substantive related direction in body, brain and quantitative health. Its anatomy, physiology, neuroscience and perception-and-action courses develop foundations relevant to movement, supported by mathematical and data methods. Dedicated biomechanics, exercise-training and clinical movement laboratories remain important gaps; the general methods courses do not guarantee movement-specific projects.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 120 EC of required first- and second-year study, 6 EC of advanced movement-system anatomy, a 24 EC research project and 30 EC of open minor or elective space. Specific sport or clinical minors are optional. Research is conducted in teams of at least two with individual reports. Entry requires completion of year one and Statistics, plus the measurement-course practical and at least 4.0 in its written exam. The usual first-year advice requirement is 42 EC, with at least 4.0 in Biomechanics and Mathematics. Language assessment and applicable remediation, practical attendance and choice-approval rules also apply.
